page: Amazon Web Services d2.8xlarge is a dense storage instance featuring 36 vCPUs and 18 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor running at 2.4 GHz. Built on the Xen hypervisor, this x86_64 architecture server includes 244.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.78 GB per core. The defining hardware characteristic is its massive local storage capacity, consisting of 49,152 GB of local HDD storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is consistently low, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scores falling into the bottom 10% tier. However, multi-core capabilities scale to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains in the middle 50% tier. LLM inference tasks perform poorly, with text generation on a 135M model and prompt processing on a 70B model ranking in the bottom 10%.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the d2.8xlarge offers high storage density per resource unit, trading off high-speed solid-state performance for massive, lower-cost HDD capacity. This makes it suitable for workloads requiring large sequential read and write operations on massive datasets where SSD speeds are not strictly required. Appropriate workloads include MapReduce logging, large-scale data warehousing, Hadoop MapReduce clusters, and massive sequential-access database storage.
